stem: A quality inspector compares two production lines. Line A produces components with a mean diameter of 200 mm and a standard deviation of 40 mm. Line B produces components with a mean diameter of 150 mm and a standard deviation of 45 mm. Which production line shows greater relative variability, and what is its coefficient of variation?

per_option_rationale.rationale: CV_A = (40/200)*100 = 20%. CV_B = (45/150)*100 = 30%. Since CV_B > CV_A, Line B has greater relative variability, with CV = 30%.

Line A has the higher absolute standard deviation only if compared incorrectly. CV_A = 20% and CV_B = 30%, so Line A does NOT have greater relative variability. The student may have compared absolute SDs (45 > 40) and incorrectly assigned the result to Line A.
CV_B = 30% not 20%. An arithmetic slip of computing 45/150 = 0.20 (forgetting to compute it as 30/100 = 0.3) leads to CV_B = 20%.
Line A has CV = 20%, not 30%. The student may have inverted the formula, computing (mean/SD)*100 = (200/40)*100 for a wrong figure, or confused which line has higher CV.

explanation: Coefficient of variation compares relative dispersion across datasets with different means. CV_A = (SD_A / mean_A) * 100 = (40/200)*100 = 20%. CV_B = (SD_B / mean_B) * 100 = (45/150)*100 = 30%. Since 30% > 20%, Line B shows greater relative variability. The setup decision is recognising that absolute SD comparison (45 > 40) is misleading when means differ.

explanation_sections.punchline: Relative variability is measured by CV, not by absolute SD; a larger SD with a larger mean can still mean less relative spread.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: relative dispersion comparison using CV = (SD/mean)*100. Compute for each: CV_A = 40/200 * 100 = 20%; CV_B = 45/150 * 100 = 30%. Identify: CV_B > CV_A, so Line B has greater relative variability. The key setup decision is choosing CV over absolute SD for the comparison.
explanation_sections.lesson: When comparing variability across groups with different means, always use CV rather than raw standard deviation; the group with the smaller mean can have higher relative spread even with a smaller absolute SD.
explanation_sections.timing: 60-75 seconds. Trap: comparing absolute SDs (45 > 40) and wrongly concluding Line B has higher absolute and Line A lower, then mixing up which answer to state.
